articles.title: EXL acquires physical AI model developer iMerit
articles.summary: EXL completed its acquisition of iMerit Technology, combining EXL’s enterprise data and industry workflow expertise with iMerit’s AI model training, evaluation, reinforcement learning, and multimodal data annotation capabilities. The companies position the deal as a way to help enterprises move AI from pilots to production by improving trust, domain-specific performance, safety, and compliance, including in robotics and autonomous systems.
articles.advisor_relevance: This acquisition highlights a shift in AI value creation from simply building large models toward making AI reliable, governed, and usable in real enterprise workflows. It is relevant for advisor conversations because it points to second-derivative beneficiaries in AI services, data quality, model evaluation, compliance, and physical AI enablement, particularly as enterprises and robotics developers seek production-ready systems.

articles.title: Deere faces headwinds in Q3 update and announces Reservoir R&D partnership
articles.summary: Deere reported Q3 2026 net income of $1.379 billion, beating expectations, and raised full-year net income guidance to $4.75 billion to $5 billion despite weakness in its Production and Precision Agriculture segment. The company also announced a $10 million, three-year R&D partnership with Reservoir to accelerate rugged AI and robotics technologies for high-value crop agriculture. Deere expects autonomous capabilities, automated spraying, and connected fleet software to support margins as the farm equipment cycle stabilizes.
articles.advisor_relevance: This article highlights Deere’s effort to use AI, autonomy, and connected software as margin-supporting growth drivers during a cyclical downturn in farm equipment demand. The Reservoir partnership is small in dollar terms but strategically relevant because it focuses on real-world commercialization of rugged AI systems, a key adoption hurdle for robotics in agriculture. For advisor conversations, Deere offers a concrete example of physical AI moving beyond the lab into labor-constrained industrial workflows.

articles.title: Hugging Face Unveils Microduck: A $399 Open-Source 25 cm Biped You Train with Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: Hugging Face’s Pollen Robotics team opened pre-orders for Microduck, a 25 cm bipedal robot priced at $399. The robot includes 15 motors, a camera, LiDAR, two IMUs, and an Apache-2.0 training stack that lets users train neural movement policies in MuJoCo and export them to ONNX.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early but concrete signal that robotics development tools are becoming cheaper, more open, and more accessible. While Microduck itself is likely a developer and research product rather than a near-term mass-market platform, it highlights broader trends in physical AI, simulation-based training, and the potential expansion of robotics ecosystems beyond large industrial players.
